section.title: Introduction
section.para: A stemmer reduces a word form to a shorter root. OpenNLP ships rule-based engines such as Snowball and Porter through the opennlp.tools.stemmer.Stemmer interface. Stemming is language-specific and lossy: it is useful for search and feature reduction, not as a substitute for lemmatization when a dictionary form is required.

section.title: StemmerFactory
Sharing and caching
section.para:
Some stemmer implementations keep mutable engine state and must not be called from several threads at once. SharingStemmer wraps a StemmerFactory and routes each call to a per-thread delegate, so one instance can be shared safely. CachingStemmer adds a bounded per-thread LRU cache of word-to-stem mappings on top of the same factory pattern. Both wrappers return the same stem as a fresh factory stemmer for the same word:
StemmerFactory factory = new SnowballStemmerFactory(SnowballStemmer.ALGORITHM.ENGLISH);
new SharingStemmer(factory).stem("running"); // "run" new CachingStemmer(factory).stem("running"); // "run"
Thread-safe stemmers such as the shareable SnowballStemmer class do not need SharingStemmer. Long-running containers should call clearThreadLocalState() when a pooled thread no longer uses a sharing or caching stemmer.

section.title: Hunspell dictionaries
section.para:
opennlp.tools.stemmer.hunspell loads a user-supplied .aff affix file and its .dic word list. OpenNLP bundles no dictionary data; dictionaries are downloaded separately, and each provides license information. Retain the dictionary's copyright notices and license text with downloaded files. OpenNLP's Apache License does not relicense those files. The dictionary is immutable and safe to share; HunspellStemmerFactory creates a fresh stemmer per call. HunspellManualExampleTest asserts the behavior shown here.
HunspellDictionary dictionary = HunspellDictionary.load( Path.of("dictionary.aff"), Path.of("dictionary.dic")); Stemmer stemmer = new HunspellStemmerFactory(dictionary).newStemmer();
stemmer.stem("workers"); // "work" stemmer.stem("table"); // "table" (unknown vocabulary is unchanged)
The stems above are those of the project-authored miniature dictionary the test loads, which lists work with an agentive and a plural suffix; the test asserts the same stem for worker. Which stem a published dictionary yields for a given form is decided by that dictionary. Acquisition helpers and the supported affix feature set live in dev/README-hunspell-dictionaries.md.

An opt-in catalog download accepts an application-supplied DictionaryCatalog, needs -Dopennlp.download.remote=true, and fetches through the digest-verified ResourceInstaller path. A file that already exists in the target is not replaced. Remove old files before refreshing a dictionary.

ICONV and OCONV convert input and output; IGNORE removes configured characters. KEEPCASE, CHECKSHARPS, and language-specific lowercase mappings govern case variants. COMPLEXPREFIXES permits 2 prefixes and 1 suffix instead of 1 prefix and 2 suffixes. Compound rules, boundary checks, simplified junctions, and recursive BREAK separators return recognized part stems in order, without duplicates. Morphological st: fields supply explicit stems, ds: suffixes make the derived form the stem, and sp: fields prepend surface material. AM expands morphology aliases. Rules that add and strip no material are undone like any other rule. The first listed homonym decides whether a spelling is forbidden, and a forbidden direct or affixed reading also blocks compound and BREAK readings. SYLLABLENUM applies Hungarian compound syllable adjustments. The deprecated LEMMA_PRESENT directive is accepted without changing results. OpenNLP does not generate inflected forms or spelling suggestions, and the morphological fields of an analysis are not part of the public API; the stemmer returns stems.

Hunspell's spell checker and its analyzer can disagree: the analyzer may return stems for a word the spell checker rejects, or no stem for a word it accepts. OpenNLP has one engine, which either recognizes a word and returns its stems or returns the word unchanged. Its recognition mostly matches Hunspell's spell checker and its stems mostly match Hunspell's analyzer; the differences are listed below. The Hunspell tests record Hunspell's result for each fixture and name each difference, and HunspellCompatibilityEval in opennlp-eval-tests records each expected difference on published dictionaries.

listitem.para: Compound stems are the stems of the recognized parts, in order. Hunspell's analyzer returns at most one stem for the whole compound, so riverboats gives river and boat here and riverboat in Hunspell. A closing part without an affix is left out of Hunspell's stem, so riverboat itself gives river there.

Purely numeric tokens such as 1.5 or 42-42 are accepted by Hunspell's spell checker before any dictionary lookup. Here they are unknown input and are returned unchanged. Recognize numbers in the tokenizer or before stemming.

A word starting with a dotted capital I is lowercased with Unicode mapping outside the Turkic languages, so İnvite is recognized when invite is listed. Hunspell's spell checker never tries the lowercase form of such a word without a Turkic LANG. Declare LANG tr, az, or crh for Turkic data, where both implementations keep the dotted and dotless letters apart.

A compound of three or more parts that is one edit away from a listed word, such as sunsetlamp next to bunsetlamp, is rejected by Hunspell's spell checker through its suggester, which OpenNLP does not provide. Such compounds are recognized here. An application that needs the rejection can validate multi-part compounds with a spelling checker, or limit COMPOUNDWORDMAX in the affix file where the language allows.
All-uppercase Turkish words such as İPEK are recognized with the stem İpek. Hunspell's spell checker rejects them, while its analyzer returns that stem.

Mixed-case words with a capitalized initial and BREAK forms are accepted by Hunspell's spell checker, but its analyzer returns no stem. OpenNLP returns the stem of the entry, such as eMarket for RaMarket, and the stems of the parts of a BREAK form, such as river and boat for rivers-boats.
Forbidden affixed compounds are rejected by Hunspell's spell checker, while its analyzer stems them. OpenNLP does not recognize them and returns them unchanged.
An affix file without SET is read as UTF-8 and rejected when it is not valid UTF-8; Hunspell's default is ISO-8859-1. Add SET ISO8859-1 to such a file.

Malformed declarations are rejected where Hunspell's parser guesses: a multi-character flag under the default flag mode, an AF or AM table whose entry count does not match its header, and a numeric flag outside 1 through 65535. Correct the declaration; ALLOW_PARTIAL skips unsupported directives, not malformed ones.

section.para: FLAG and AF declarations apply to the complete affix file, including rules listed before those declarations. Parsing rejects malformed text in parsed rules, invalid counts, numeric flags outside the range 1 through 65535, and COMPOUNDMIN values that cannot be doubled safely. Comments and unused metadata may retain a legacy encoding. Default and long flag modes preserve raw one-byte flag values in UTF-8 files. Compound length and boundary checks count Unicode code points. A rule that strips a whole stem applies only when the affix file declares FULLSTRIP, as in Hunspell itself. Each affix or dictionary stream is rejected when it exceeds HunspellDictionary.MAX_STREAM_BYTES (64 MiB). Search permits at most 64 compound components, 2048 compound candidate checks per case variant, and 2048 word-break attempts per input. Sharp-s expansion permits at most 64 case variants. Output is limited to 2048 distinct results. Compound-rule patterns permit 4096 flag elements. Simplified triple letters can be restored at multiple junctions; CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN replacement applies at one junction. These limits can exclude valid analyses; candidates must pass validation before inclusion in the result.
